Towards the formal verification of autonomous agent teams\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1049/ic:20050184\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2005]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1049/ic:20050177\", \"title\": [\"Principles, architectures and trends in autonomous control\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1049/ic:20050177\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2005]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.65109/tmlz4501\", \"title\": [\"State-Space Reduction Techniques in Agent Verification\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>We have developed a set of tools to allow the use of model-checking techniques for the verification of systems directly implemented in an agent-oriented programming language. The success of model checking as a verification technique for large systems is dependent partly on its use in combination with various state-space reduction techniques. An important example of such techniques is property-based slicing. This paper introduces an algorithm for property-based slicing of AgentSpeak multi-agent systems. We apply our approach to the AgentSpeak code for a scenario inspired by routine tasks of autonomous Mars rovers, and explain how slicing reduces the search space in theory. We consider experiments on such scenarios, and initial results show a significant reduction in the state space, thus indicating that this approach can have an important impact on the practicality of agent verification.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.65109/tmlz4501\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2004, 7, 19]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "22fd0be4436dd6364c5b402c5365363dd58ed420575f52cc9f14a96b4ffe0dd3", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_problem", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.70729/ijser15932", "doi:10.1049/ic:20050184", "doi:10…
